articles.title: Claude Code Batch File Edits: Using MultiEdit and Write Together to Cut Round-Trips in Long Refactor Sessions
articles.excerpt: Claude Code Batch File Edits: Using MultiEdit and Write Together to Cut Round-Trips in Long Refactor Sessions This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. Mo…
articles.body: Claude Code Batch File Edits: Using MultiEdit and Write Together to Cut Round-Trips in Long Refactor Sessions This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. Most Claude Code refactors burn tokens on sequential file edits that wait for confirmation after each change. The pattern looks like this: the LLM applies an edit to one file, sends the patch, waits for the user to approve, then repeats for the next file. A rename that touches fifteen modules becomes fifteen separate round-trips. Each trip adds latency, consumes output tokens for boilerplate responses, and risks breaking atomicity if the user cancels midway through.

articles.body: Upload a malicious SVG to the admin product image field and get stored XSS that fires for every visitor. The admin panel in OopsSec Store lets you upload product images, including SVGs. Since SVG is just XML, you can embed a <script> tag in one, upload it as a product image, and the JavaScript runs in the browser of anyone who views that product. Prerequisites You need admin access. articles.title: Disk full? broot's whale-spotting mode plus Ctrl-G turns your cleanup into one command
articles.excerpt: Every engineer knows the disk-full afternoon. The build or the backup job fails, and you end up in the same loop using du -sh and rm: du -sh */ | sort -h rm that-one-cache-dir du -sh */ | sort -h rm a…
articles.body: Every engineer knows the disk-full afternoon. The build or the backup job fails, and you end up in the same loop using du -sh and rm : du -sh * / | sort -h rm that-one-cache-dir du -sh * / | sort -h rm another-thing That works but, since the listing you get is flat, you see directory totals, not the files inside them. And you delete one directory at a time, with no way to collect a set of files, review the set, and delete it in one go. This article is about a workflow I use instead, built on broot's staging area: br -w lists files sorted by size, Ctrl-G collects the files you want to delete into a review panel, :rm deletes the whole set. Let's explore the details, while running the workflow in a real directory.

articles.body: Hello, I'm Rijul, and I'm building LiveReview — a blast-radius aware AI code review built for your business-critical systems. Star us to help devs discover the project, give it a try, and share your feedback to help improve the product. If you have read about RAG, you will probably be familiar with the concept of embeddings . We take a bunch of text and turn it into numbers. That's it. But there is one more layer here. There are different ways to represent text for retrieval. Two important approaches are sparse representations and dense embeddings . Let's understand how they work and when each one is useful. articles.title: Hubble Spots Chaotic Secret in Galaxy
articles.excerpt: A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way gal…
articles.body: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Thilker, the MAUVE-HST Team A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disk of stars, gas, and dust. These arms are marked by opaque clumps of brown dust and dotted with small collections of bright blue stars. Unlike many other spiral galaxies, NGC 4698’s delicate spiral arms are only prominent in the outer reaches of the disk; spiral arms often wind down to the very center of a galaxy, but NGC 4698’s spiral arms appear to shy away from its glowing center. The arms instead hover in a ring-like structure around the perimeter of the galaxy.
